newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Short-dated mark calls bid as dlr slides. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short-dated mark calls bid as dlr slides. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects in title and story to "mark calls" from "mark puts")
Shorter-dated mark calls in dollar/mark options were well bid as spot extended its retracement from last week's highs in the U.S., traders said.
Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, flipped in favor of mark calls in the one- and two-week area.
"One-month risk reversal is awfully close to doing the same," said MaryBeth Slack, FX options analyst at MCM OptionWatch.
Risk reversals for one-month and out had been favoring mark puts for most of the year, particularly steadily in recent months as the dollar marched relentlessly higher.

The dollar, which had risen to within a whisker of 1.90 marks last week, tumbled below 1.83 marks in the U.S. on news of the Bundesbank's hawkish assessment on German inflation. Speculation about a delay in European economic and monetary union stemming from a British newspaper report also added pressure on dollar/mark.
Dollar/mark implied volatilities were initially lower in Asia and Europe but bounced back as the dollar's decline accelerated in the U.S.
One-month volatility stood at 11.1/11.3 percent at U.S. midsession, little changed from late Tuesday levels.

A U.S. bank trader in New York said the middle part of the curve was soft, while the front end was buoyed by the sharp spot selloff and the back end was underpinned by demand from die-hard dollar bulls.
"There were a ton of buyers of the short-dated stuff, but it didn't really go beyond two weeks," he said, noting that the two- to four-month area was relatively under pressure.

"It looks like the options market isn't particularly worried about the dollar falling out of bed," he added. "If anything, it looks like it's expecting the dollar to either calm down or maybe even drift higher in the longer term."
Dollar/yen volatilities were soft, with the curve steepening its modestly positive slope.
Although spot dollar/yen slipped in sympathy with dollar/mark, the dollar held in the lower 115-yen area, well above last Friday's 114.25-yen low.
One-month volatility stood at 11.3/11.5 percent at U.S. midday, off a quarter point from Tuesday. One-year was steadier at 11.6/11.8 percent.
One-week options were well bid, perhaps due to the August 19 Federal Open Market Committee meeting and nervous, volatile U.S. asset markets, traders noted.
Dollar/yen risk reversals were little changed, favoring yen calls in the shorter dates. They had come in toward par earlier but widened back out as the dollar fell below 116 yen.
Sterling/mark volatilities spiked up again as sterling sank deeper and fell below 2.9 marks, compared with late July highs above 3.08 marks.
One-month sterling/mark jumped to 12.5/13.0 percent from Tuesday's 11.9/12.3 percent. One-week was near 15 percent.
Elsewhere, back-end dollar/Swiss franc volatilities came off relative to dollar/mark, perhaps as a function of the mark's EMU divergence trades, traders said.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: chicago.derivatives.newsroom@reuters.com
